  • Referral program — bonuses for clients you invite.

docs.title: How a slot is fulfilled
docs.text:
Once an order is published, each slot goes through its own path: it waits for an executor, the executor takes it and starts the verification on the exchange, the exchange reviews the verification, and the slot is completed. If an attempt fails but the exchange hasn't refused for good, the executor retries on their own — you don't need to do anything. If the executor doesn't finish within the time they're given, the slot goes back to the queue and another executor takes it (see Change of executor).

All you need to do is upload the accounts and publish the order, and later update a slot's data if the platform asks you to.

docs.title: Slot statuses
docs.text:
Status in the bot In the web app What it means What you do 📥 Waiting for upload Awaiting upload No account has been uploaded to the slot yet Upload an account 📤 Account uploaded Awaiting upload The account was accepted, but the order still has empty slots Upload the rest 📤 Ready to publish Ready to publish Every slot in the order has an account Publish the order 🕓 Awaiting executor Waiting for a worker The order is published, and the slot is waiting for an executor — Status unchanged, with "🧊 This slot is waiting for renewal…" above the card Frozen Your subscription has expired: until you renew, the slot isn't offered to executors Renew the subscription or cancel the slot 🔄 In progress In progress An executor has taken the slot and is completing the verification — ⏳ Under review Verifying The exchange is reviewing the verification; clocks are paused — 🔄 Attempt failed — the worker is retrying Attempt failed The exchange rejected the attempt, and the executor is trying again — ⚠️ Data update required Resubmit required A fresh proxy, fresh cookies or both are needed; the slot is paused Update the data 📸 Waiting for face check Waiting for face check MEXC: the verification has passed, and the platform is waiting to see whether the exchange asks for a face check — 🔄 In progress Face check MEXC has asked for a face check, and the executor is completing it — ✔️ Completed Completed The verification has passed — 🚫 Cancelled Cancelled The slot is closed; the money for it has usually been refunded —

Re-verifications use the same statuses; Risk Removal has its own, described on the Risk Removal on MEXC page.

The slot card shows the slot's status, its next deadline, its event history and, once the slot is closed, its outcome — for example, "✔️ Passed" or the reason for cancellation (see Cancellations and refunds).

docs.title: Order status
docs.text:
An order's status follows the statuses of its slots:

  • before publishing — "📥 Waiting for account upload" or "📤 Ready to publish";
  • after publishing — "🔄 In progress", as long as at least one slot is still open;
  • once every slot is closed — "✔️ Completed" (all completed), "✔️ Partially completed" (some completed) or "🚫 Cancelled" (none completed).

For a published order, the counters on the order card show where the slots are right now: "🔄 In work", "🕓 Waiting for a worker", "❄️ Frozen", "✔️ Done", "🚫 Cancelled". When a slot moves from one executor to another, the order status doesn't change — only the counters do. If the order had any refunds, the card shows a "💸 Refunded to your balance: $…" line — even while the order is still in progress.

docs.title: Fulfillment deadline
docs.text:
You choose a slot's deadline when you buy an initial verification — standard, wholesale or team:

  • "No deadline" — the slot is never cancelled for running out of time and waits until it's completed;
  • 4, 8, 12, 24, 48 or 72 hours; in the web app, "Other…" lets you enter any whole number of hours from 4 to 72.

The price doesn't depend on your choice. The deadline can't be changed after purchase. Re-verifications and Risk Removal have no deadline.

How the deadline is counted:

  • it starts when the order is published, not when an executor takes the slot;
  • it belongs to the slot: if the slot passes to another executor, the countdown doesn't restart;
  • it stops while the exchange is reviewing the verification ("⏳ Under review"), while the slot is waiting for you to update its data, and while the slot is frozen. After a pause, the deadline moves forward by the length of the pause;
  • on MEXC, once the exchange has confirmed the verification, the order deadline no longer applies — from then on, only the observation period deadlines apply.

The current deadline is shown on the slot card: "⏳ Slot deadline: …" (in the web app, "Verification deadline" with a countdown). While the exchange is reviewing the verification, the card says "⏳ The deadline does not apply: waiting for the exchange's answer."; while the slot is waiting for data, it says "⏸ The deadline is paused — waiting for the session update."

docs.title: When the deadline passes
docs.text:
• If no verification link has been issued to an executor yet, the slot is cancelled right away and the money is refunded to your balance.
  • If a link has been issued, the executor gets 10 more minutes, after which the platform checks the exchange itself. Meanwhile, the card says "⚠️ The time allowed ran out…". Then:
    • the verification has passed — the slot counts as completed;
    • it hasn't passed — the slot is cancelled and the money is refunded to your balance; the outcome on the card is "⌛ Deadline expired";
    • the exchange is still reviewing the verification — the slot moves to "⏳ Under review" and isn't cancelled until a response comes in;
    • the exchange couldn't be checked because the proxy or session stopped working — the platform asks you to update the data, and the check runs after that;
    • the exchange didn't respond for another reason — the slot isn't cancelled until a response comes in.

docs.title: Change of executor
docs.text:
An executor who takes an initial verification slot gets 4 hours of their own time for it. That time stops while the exchange is reviewing the verification or the slot is waiting for your data, and nothing the executor does extends it. If they don't make it, the slot goes back to the queue for another executor, and the one who ran out of time can't take that slot again.

While an executor holds the slot, the card shows the moment they have to finish by: "⏳ The worker has until … — otherwise the slot goes back to the pool for another worker." (in the web app, "Back to the pool by … at the latest if the worker doesn't finish"). If your deadline comes first, the card shows that instead.

A slot also goes back to the queue if the executor turns it down or an administrator takes them off it. If the executor ran out of time or turned the slot down after issuing a verification link, the slot doesn't leave at once: the platform waits 10 minutes and checks the exchange — a passed verification counts. For you, a return looks like this: the slot is back to "🕓 Awaiting executor", the order status doesn't change, your deadline carries on from where it was, and nothing is cancelled. A verification passed through the previous executor's link still counts later on. For details, see Executor's time and returning a slot to the pool.

For team orders, you set the executor's time yourself: "⚙️ Settings" → "⏱ Worker's time" in the workspace bot, or "Settings" → "Worker's time per slot" in the web app — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours, or "No limit" (see Worker's time per slot). Re-verifications have no executor's time: a re-verification stays with the executor who did the initial verification.

docs.title: MEXC observation period
docs.text:
MEXC often asks for a repeat face check right after the initial verification. That's why a MEXC slot isn't completed as soon as the verification succeeds:

  • For 30 minutes, the platform monitors the account. During this time the slot shows as "📸 Waiting for face check", and the bot sends you a message that KYC has passed. If the exchange doesn't request a face check, the slot completes automatically.
  • If the exchange does request a face check, the executor has 12 hours to pass it. This costs you nothing. Meanwhile, the bot shows the slot as "🔄 In progress", and the web app as "Face check". If the slot is waiting for you to update its data, those 12 hours are paused.
  • If the executor doesn't make it in time, the platform checks the exchange: the face check has passed — the slot completes; it hasn't — the slot is cancelled and the money is refunded to your balance.

Once MEXC has confirmed the initial verification, the order deadline and the executor's time no longer apply. You don't need to do anything.

docs.title: Frozen slots
docs.text:
Freezing applies only to wholesale and team orders for initial verification. When your subscription expires:

  • slots of published orders that no executor holds right now are frozen: until you renew, we don't offer them to executors;
  • slots already in progress are completed as usual. If such a slot goes back to the queue, it freezes too, and you get a message about it;
  • uploading, replacing accounts, re-uploading, checking status and publishing all keep working. You can publish an unpublished order, but its slots are frozen straight away — the order card warns you about this;
  • while a slot is frozen, its deadline doesn't run: after you renew, the deadline moves forward by the time the slot was frozen;
  • frozen slots are never cancelled on their own — they wait for your renewal as long as it takes.

On the order card, frozen slots are counted under "❄️ Frozen". In the bot, the card of such a slot has "🧊 This slot is waiting for renewal…" above it; in the web app, its status is "Frozen".

What you can do:

  • "Renew subscription" — the slots are offered to executors again;
  • "Cancel frozen" on the order card — for slots where no verification link was issued, the money is refunded right away; where one was, the exchange is checked first. For details, see Cancellations and refunds.

Standard orders and re-verifications are never frozen. For how freezing works on team orders, see When your subscription ends.

docs.title: Checking the status
docs.text:
The "🔍 Check status" button on the slot card ("Check status" in the web app) asks the exchange for the current state of the verification — or, on MEXC during an additional face check, the state of that check. The check works the same way as the executor's: if the exchange confirms success, the slot counts as completed, no matter who tapped the button.

The button is there when the slot has an account and a proxy uploaded, and the slot is:

  • not yet taken by an executor — including before publishing;
  • in progress, with the executor having already started the verification on the exchange;
  • under review by the exchange, or after a failed attempt;
  • going through an additional face check on MEXC.

It isn't available while an executor has taken the slot but hasn't started the verification yet, while the slot is waiting for a data update, during the 30-minute MEXC observation period, on completed and cancelled slots, or at the Risk Removal stages. You can check the same slot again after 30 seconds at the earliest.

If the check finds a problem with the data on a published order:

  • the session has expired or the proxy doesn't respond — the slot moves to "⚠️ Data update required" (see Re-uploading);
  • the proxy works, but the exchange doesn't open through it — you can replace the proxy yourself.

Before publishing, just replace the slot's data instead.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
The bot notifies you about key events:

  • a slot is waiting for a data update — for one slot or as a summary for several; if the data hasn't arrived after 6 hours, you get one reminder;
  • a MEXC verification has passed and the observation period has started;
  • a slot has been completed or cancelled (with the reason and the refund amount);
  • a whole order has been completed;
  • the check of uploaded accounts has finished, if the bot didn't wait for its result in the dialog;
  • your subscription is about to expire or has expired, slots have been frozen, or they're offered to executors again after you renew (see Subscription);
  • a top-up has been detected and credited;
  • a referral bonus has been credited.

In the web app ("Settings" → "Notifications"), you can turn "Per slot", "Per order", "Deposits" and "Referral bonuses" notifications on or off separately. Requests to update data and subscription messages always come through, as does the outcome of a cancellation you asked for yourself. You can also turn off referral bonus notifications in the workspace bot, in the "🎟️ Referrals" section.

docs.title: Orders and slots
docs.text:
An order is a single purchase: an exchange, a country and a number of verifications. A slot is one account within an order: an order for five verifications has five slots. Slots are fulfilled independently of each other — one may already be completed while another is still waiting for an executor. The order's status is derived from the statuses of its slots (see Order statuses).

An order and each of its slots have their own number, which looks like 1234-5678. Use it to find an order or when you contact support.

docs.title: Order types
docs.text:
Type Price Fulfilled by Requirement Standard Retail, from the catalog Platform executors from the order's country — Wholesale Discounted, from the catalog Platform executors from the order's country An active subscription Team You set it; the full amount goes to the executor Only members of your team An active subscription and at least one active team member Re-verification Under the re-verification pricing rules The executor who did the account's first verification The account was already verified through the platform

Standard and wholesale orders are the same catalog product at two different prices. How to order a re-verification is covered on the Re-verifications page.

docs.title: Where to place an order
docs.text: Type Shop bot Workspace bot Web app Standard Yes The button takes you to the shop bot Yes Wholesale — Yes Yes Team — Yes Yes Re-verification — Yes Yes

docs.title: Shop bot @kyctrade_bot
docs.text:
1. Open "🛍 Catalog", choose an exchange, then a country.
  2. Check the product card: the price per slot, a description and, where available, a guide, the working hours of executors in that country (outside those hours, there may be delays) and the prices of re-verifications for that country.
  3. Tap "🛒 Buy" and enter the quantity. The number of slots in a single order is limited.
  4. On the confirmation screen, check the total and your balance, optionally choose a slot deadline, and tap "✅ Confirm".
  5. The payment is deducted from your balance right away. If you don't have enough funds, the bot replies "Insufficient balance." — top up your balance and try again. If the price has changed in the meantime, the bot shows the new total and asks you to confirm again.
  6. The bot shows the order number and an "📤 Upload accounts" button, which opens the upload in the workspace bot.

If a product is temporarily unavailable, the card shows "⛔️ Currently out of stock". Tap "🔔 Notify when available", and the bot will let you know when you can place the order.

docs.title: Workspace bot @kycportal_bot
docs.text:
"➕ New order" offers three options: "Wholesale", "Standard" (takes you to the shop bot) and "For my team".

  • Wholesale — choose the exchange and country, tap "🛒 Buy", enter the quantity and confirm. Without an active subscription, the product card shows "💳 Get a subscription" instead of "🛒 Buy".
  • For my team — choose the exchange and any country, then set the price per slot and the quantity; see Your own team for details.

You can choose a slot deadline on the confirmation screen of wholesale and team orders too. If your subscription ends in less than 24 hours, the bot warns you: slots that no executor has taken by then will stop being offered to executors until you renew (see When your subscription ends). It's only a warning — you can still place the order.

Re-verifications are ordered through "🔄 Re-verification".

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
1. Open "Create order" and choose a mode: "Catalog", "Team" or "Reverification". In the catalog, with an active subscription you can choose the price — "Standard" or "Wholesale"; without one, the subscription price is shown next to the standard price.
  2. Choose the exchange and country, and enter the quantity and, for a team order, the price per slot. Optionally set a "Slot deadline" (see below).
  3. Review the summary — quantity, total and your balance after payment — then tap "Pay" and confirm. If you don't have enough funds, the web app shows how much you're short and offers to top up. If your subscription ends in less than 24 hours, you'll see the same warning as in the bot.
  4. After payment, a screen with the new order opens, with "Upload accounts" and "View order" buttons.

docs.title: Slot deadline
docs.text:
When you buy a standard, wholesale or team order, you can set a deadline by which each slot must pass verification:

  • in the bots — with the buttons on the confirmation screen: "No deadline", "4 h", "8 h", "12 h", "24 h", "48 h" or "72 h";
  • in the web app — in the "Slot deadline" step: the same options, or "Other…" for any whole number of hours from 4 to 72.

The deadline counts from the moment the order is published and is the same for all its slots. You can't change it after purchase, and it doesn't affect the price. If verification hasn't passed by the deadline, the slot is cancelled and the money returns to your balance. Without a deadline, a slot is never cancelled for running out of time. For how the deadline runs, see Order execution and deadlines.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text:
After payment, the order waits for you to upload accounts (see Uploading accounts). Executors can't see the order until you publish it:

  1. Upload a session and proxy to every slot in the order. You can't publish part of an order: a slot without an account or without a proxy will stop the order from being published.
  2. The order status changes to "📤 Ready to publish". Until you publish, you can open any slot and replace its account.
  3. Tap "✅ Publish now" and confirm with "🚀 Confirm & publish" (in the web app, "Publish order" → "Publish").

If your subscription has already ended, you can still publish a wholesale or team order, but its slots will be frozen right away until you renew — the order card warns you about this with "🧊 Subscription expired — once published, the slots stay frozen until it is renewed." (see When your subscription ends).

Once the order is published, you can't change a slot's session or proxy at will. You can update the data when the platform itself asks for it on a specific slot, and replace the proxy when a check shows that the proxy works but the exchange doesn't open through it — the slot card then shows "🔌 Replace proxy" (see Re-uploading). An unpublished order can be cancelled as a whole with a full refund — see Cancellations and refunds.

docs.title: Where to see your orders
docs.text:
• Workspace bot — "📋 My orders": the "Active", "Completed" and "Re-KYC" (re-verifications) tabs, plus "🔍 Search" by order number, slot number or the account's full email address. An order card shows its status, slot counters (see below), the refunded amount if there was a refund, its slots and the available actions; a slot card shows its status, deadline and event history.
  • Web app — "Orders": the "Active" and "Completed" tabs, search by order or slot number, filters by status, exchange, country, type and period, and a "Needs attention" view — orders with slots waiting for you to update their data. "Slots" is a single list of every account across all your orders, searchable by slot number, order number or the full account. In the web app, each order has a full event history.
  • Shop bot — "👤 Profile" → "📋 My Orders": a short list of your purchases.

docs.title: Order statuses
docs.text:
An order's status shows only its overall stage:

Status What it means 📥 Waiting for account upload The order is paid, but not every slot has an account yet 📤 Ready to publish Every slot has an account, and the order is waiting to be published 🔄 In progress The order is published, and not all of its slots are closed yet ✔️ Completed All slots are done ✔️ Partially completed All slots are closed: some were done, some were cancelled 🚫 Cancelled All slots are closed and none was done

While an order is "🔄 In progress", its status doesn't change when executors take slots or slots go back to the pool. The counters on the order card show where each slot is right now:

  • "🔄 In work: N" — slots an executor is working on;
  • "🕓 Waiting for a worker: N" — slots nobody has taken at the moment;
  • "❄️ Frozen: N" — slots waiting for you to renew your subscription;
  • "✔️ Done: N" and "🚫 Cancelled: N".

There's no separate status for a refund. If money came back for the order — for a cancelled order or just for some of its slots — the card shows a "💸 Refunded to your balance: $…" line.

The web app shows the same statuses and counters without icons; the shop bot shows statuses with its own icons, sometimes with slightly different wording. Statuses of individual slots are described on the Order execution and deadlines page.

docs.title: Platform overview
docs.text: KYC Portal helps you pass verification (KYC) on crypto exchanges. You buy a verification for the exchange and country you need, then give the platform the account's session (cookies) and a proxy. An executor from the order's country completes the verification using a link that the platform generates inside your session. The platform takes care of the rest: assigning slots to executors, checking the result on the exchange, notifications and refunds.

docs.title: Supported exchanges
docs.text:
• Bybit
  • MEXC
  • KuCoin

The catalog shows the available countries and prices for each exchange — in the shop bot and in the web app.

docs.title: Where to use the platform
docs.text:
Where What for Shop bot @kyctrade_bot Browsing the catalog and buying at standard prices, your standard orders, topping up your balance, your referral link Workspace bot @kycportal_bot Uploading accounts, publishing and tracking orders, wholesale and team orders, re-verifications, your team, subscription, settings, signing in to the web app Web app Everything in the workspace bot, plus catalog purchases, full transaction history, analytics and choosing executors

Your account, balance, orders and interface language are shared across both bots and the web app: anything you do in one place shows up in the others right away. There's no separate sign-up — your Telegram account is your account.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Order — a single purchase: an exchange, a country and a verification type, in the quantity you need. See Orders.
  • Slot — one account within an order. An order for three verifications has three slots; each one is fulfilled independently and has its own status.
  • Executor (called "Sellers" in the interface) — the person who passes the identity check on the exchange for your slot. Executors have no access to your account's login details. See Executors and order distribution.
  • Re-verification — a repeat check of an account that was already verified through the platform. See Re-verifications.

docs.title: How an order works
docs.text:
1. Top-up. You top up your internal balance in USDT or USDC — Balance and top-ups.
  2. Purchase. You choose the exchange, country and quantity, optionally set a slot deadline, and pay from your balance — Orders.
  3. Upload. For each slot, you provide the account's session and proxy; the platform checks them on the exchange and accepts an account only if a verification can be started on it right now — Uploading accounts.
  4. Publishing. Once every slot has an account, you publish the order and it becomes available to executors. If you set a deadline, it counts from this moment — Fulfillment deadline.
  5. Fulfillment. An executor takes a slot and completes the verification; you get notifications as the work progresses — Order execution and deadlines.
  6. Result. The slot either completes successfully or is cancelled. For when the money for a slot returns to your balance, see Cancellations and refunds.

docs.title: Referral program
docs.text: Invite people you know to KYC Portal and earn bonuses on their purchases.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Up to 10% of the price of every verification your referral buys at the standard price, once the verification has passed.
  • 10% of every subscription payment they make, including renewals.

The verification bonus depends on the product: for some products it's less than 10%. The exact amount of each bonus is shown in the bonus notification and in the list of earnings in the web app.

Bonuses are credited to your referral balance automatically. You don't earn a bonus on your referral's wholesale or team orders, re-verifications of any kind or balance top-ups.

docs.title: How to invite
docs.text:
Every client has a personal referral link. You can find yours:

  • in the shop bot @kyctrade_bot — "👤 Profile";
  • in the workspace bot @kycportal_bot — "🎟️ Referrals"; the "Invite" button lets you send an invitation to any chat straight away;
  • in the web app — the "Affiliate" section.

The person you invite opens the link and starts the bot, and they're linked to you automatically and permanently.

Note

Linking only works for new users, when they start the bot for the first time. If someone has already used the bots before, the link won't connect them to you.

docs.title: Custom link
docs.text: In the workspace bot ("✏️ Change personal link") and in the web app, you can replace the code in your link with a memorable one of your own. The code must be unique, 5 to 30 characters long and consist of Latin letters, digits and underscores, with at least one letter. Once you change the code, your old links stop working — so if you've already sent out invitations, it's best not to change it unless you have to.

docs.title: Where to see your earnings
docs.text:
• Shop bot — "👤 Profile": your referral balance, the number of people you've invited and your link.
  • Workspace bot — "🎟️ Referrals": how much you've earned in total, the number of people you've invited and your link.
  • Web app — "Affiliate": how much you've earned in total and separately from verifications and subscriptions, the number of people you've invited and how many of them have already brought you bonuses, and the list of earnings.

For every bonus, the workspace bot sends you a "💰 You received a referral reward of …$" notification. You can turn these off in the workspace bot with the "Referral reward pushes: Yes" button in "🎟️ Referrals" (once tapped, it changes to "Referral reward pushes: No"), or in the web app with the "Bonus notifications" switch in "Affiliate" or under "Settings" → "Notifications" → "Referral bonuses". It's one and the same setting: changing it in one place changes it everywhere.

docs.title: How to use your referral balance
docs.text:
You can use your referral balance to pay for any of the platform's services; when you pay, it's spent first, before your main balance (see Balance and top-ups).

Withdrawing the referral balance is available only to platform partners — on request, via "💸 Withdraw referral balance" ("👤 Profile" in the shop bot or "💵 Balance (…$)" in the workspace bot) or through support at @freidbase.

docs.title: Re-verifications
docs.text: A re-verification is a repeat check of an account that was already verified through the platform. Exchanges periodically require one for accounts that have already passed: for example, a repeat face check, an identity check before a withdrawal or before creating an API key, or the removal of restrictions. A re-verification is done by the same executor who completed the account's first verification.

docs.title: Re-verification types
docs.text:
The types are named after the matching features on the exchange itself, which makes it easier to match a platform screen with the exchange's own screen.

Exchange Type What it is MEXC Face Security A repeat face check requested by the exchange MEXC Face Withdraw A face check the exchange requests before a withdrawal MEXC Face API Key A face check the exchange requests before an API key can be created MEXC Risk Removal Lifting a Risk Control restriction — see Risk Removal on MEXC Bybit Claim Rewards Claiming the rewards available on the account

The available types depend on the exchange and may change; the current list and prices are shown when you place the order.

Face API Key. The executor only passes the face check — the platform doesn't create the API key and never sees its details. Once the slot is completed, create the key in MEXC yourself, with the code from your email and your 2FA. Don't put it off: if MEXC asks for a face check again before you've created the key, you'll need a new order.

docs.title: Which accounts are eligible
docs.text:
You can order a re-verification for an account that has a completed and successfully passed initial-verification slot on the platform. In addition:

  • the exchange must actually require the chosen check right now — the platform checks this before you pay;
  • the account mustn't already have another re-verification in progress or be busy with another active order.

The exception is MEXC: if the initial-verification slot was cancelled because the additional face check wasn't passed within 12 hours, you can only order Face Withdraw for that account.

Accounts that aren't eligible are skipped during the check, with the reason shown, and you aren't charged for them.

docs.title: How to order
docs.text: Re-verifications are ordered in batches: you can upload several accounts at once — up to 120 per batch — and see a plan with prices before you pay. Checking the accounts is free; you're only charged after you confirm.

docs.title: In the workspace bot @kycportal_bot
docs.text:
1. Open "🔄 Re-verification" and choose an exchange.
  2. Choose a type — it applies to every account in the batch.
  3. Send a list of proxies — one per account. Wait for them to be checked and tap "▶️ Continue".
  4. Send the cookie files (.json) in the same order as the proxies and tap "✅ I've sent all files".
  5. Wait for the sessions to be checked and review the plan: the accounts, the price of each one and the total.
  6. Tap "✅ Confirm & pay".

docs.title: In the web app
docs.text:
"Create order" → "Reverification": choose the exchange and type → upload the accounts the same way as in a regular upload — an ADS Power file or manually → "Check accounts" → review the plan → "Create N · $…".

If your balance didn't cover every account, the paid ones go into work straight away. For the rest, top up your balance and tap "🔄 Retry remaining" ("Retry remaining" in the web app) within 2 hours; after that you'll need to upload the accounts again.

For Risk Removal, you'll also need to provide deposit screenshots before paying — see Risk Removal on MEXC.

docs.title: Price
docs.text:
The price depends on the country and on how the original order for the account was bought, as well as on whether you have an active subscription:

Original order Active subscription No subscription Standard Retail price Retail price Wholesale Wholesale price Retail price, with an offer to renew your subscription Team You set the price per slot Can't be ordered until you renew your subscription

For accounts from team orders, you enter one price per slot for all such accounts in the batch — it goes to the executor in full.

Risk Removal costs the same for everyone — the retail price, however the original order was bought. For accounts from team orders, an active subscription is still required.

The exact amount is always shown in the plan before you pay.

docs.title: Who fulfills it
docs.text:
The slot is assigned straight to the executor who did the account's first verification and isn't shown to any other executor. If the executor is slow to start, the platform sends them a reminder. A re-verification never goes back to the shared pool under any circumstances — the slot stays with that executor until it's completed or cancelled.

If that executor isn't available, the slot isn't handed to anyone else. In a team order, if the executor is no longer on your team, you can cancel the slot right away or add the executor back to your team — the slot then goes back to them (see Cancelling a re-verification). In other cases, support handles such a slot.

docs.title: Statuses and timing
docs.text:
A re-verification has the same statuses as a regular slot (see Slot statuses); Risk Removal has its own. In the workspace bot, re-verifications are grouped under "📋 My orders" → "Re-KYC".

Unlike an initial verification, a re-verification has no fulfillment deadline. Instead, you can request a cancellation after 24 hours — the rules are described in Cancelling a re-verification.

Re-verifications are never frozen when a subscription ends: each one is a separate, paid order that is fulfilled regardless of your subscription status.

docs.title: How a re-verification ends
docs.text:
• The check passes — the slot is completed and you get a notification. For Risk Removal, the slot is completed once MEXC approves the appeal; for Face API Key, create the key yourself after that.
  • ℹ️ No check was needed — refunded — by the time the executor took up the slot, the exchange no longer required this check, and no link had been issued for the slot yet. If a link had already been issued, the slot counts as completed.
  • 🚫 Wrong country verified — the exchange confirmed the check with a different country; the slot is cancelled with a full refund.
  • The exchange refuses the check (for example, it blocks the account) — the re-verification isn't closed and isn't refunded automatically: the slot stays with the executor, and support decides what happens to it.
  • Cancellation — by you (see Cancelling a re-verification) or by support.

When a re-verification is cancelled, you get a "❌ Re-verification cancelled" notification with the reason and, if there was a refund, the amount. If you cancelled the slot and it closed right away, the result is shown on screen.

docs.title: Risk Removal on MEXC
docs.text: Risk Removal is a re-verification type for MEXC accounts that the exchange has placed under a Risk Control restriction. The platform prepares an appeal, files it with MEXC on your behalf and tracks the exchange's decision.

docs.title: What a Risk Control restriction is
docs.text: It's a protective measure on MEXC: if the exchange's anti-fraud system considers an account's activity suspicious, it restricts some operations — withdrawals, for example — until the account passes an additional check. Risk Removal is an order to have that restriction lifted.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Like any re-verification, Risk Removal can only be ordered for a MEXC account that was already verified through the platform (see Which accounts are eligible).

Before you pay, the platform checks each account for free and skips it with the reason shown — for example, if:

  • the account has no restriction — there's nothing to lift;
  • Advanced KYC isn't completed on the account — finish it in the MEXC app and try again;
  • MEXC checks faces on this account through a provider the platform doesn't work with;
  • MEXC asks for documents on this account that the platform can't file yet;
  • the account's status couldn't be read — try again in a few minutes.

docs.title: What you need to provide
docs.text:
• An active session and proxy for the account — the same as when ordering any re-verification.
  • Screenshots of the one or two most recent deposits to this account.

Everything else MEXC asks for in the appeal, the platform prepares itself.

Screenshot requirements:

  1. The screenshot shows the transfer record on the service the deposit was sent from to MEXC — not on the MEXC side.
  2. One screenshot, one transaction. The coin, amount, date and time, and TxID (transaction hash) are visible on it.
  3. If the deposit came from your own wallet (Trust Wallet, MetaMask and the like), MEXC needs two screenshots for it: the transaction and your wallet address.
  4. Use the most recent deposit. If there were no deposits in the past 90 days, an earlier one will do.
  5. Send the screenshot as a file, without compression: a regular photo in Telegram gets compressed, small text becomes blurry, and MEXC rejects screenshots like that.
  6. For each screenshot, say where the deposit came from — just the name of the service or wallet, for example Bybit or Trust Wallet. It goes into the appeal verbatim and must match the screenshot.
  7. One deposit is enough. A second deposit (MEXC accepts proof of the last 1–2) and wallet-address screenshots are added as separate steps — no more than 4 screenshots per account in total.

Warning

MEXC doesn't accept screenshots from blockchain explorers (Etherscan, Tronscan, BscScan or any others) — this is the most common reason for rejection.

docs.title: How to order
docs.text:
The steps are the same as for any re-verification (see How to order), except that after the plan, before payment, the bot or the web app asks for the deposit screenshots.

  • In the workspace bot, Risk Removal is ordered one account at a time. After the plan, tap "📎 Continue — add the screenshot", send the screenshot and write where the deposit came from. Then tap "➕ Add another screenshot" or "✅ That is all", review the summary and tap "✅ Confirm & pay".
  • In the web app, you can order up to 50 accounts at once: at the "Add screenshots" step, attach screenshots for each account and tap "Continue to payment". Accounts without screenshots are skipped, not ordered.

docs.title: What the platform does
docs.text:
After payment, the process runs automatically:

  1. If MEXC requires a face check for the appeal, the executor who did the account's first verification completes it. If it doesn't, this step is skipped.
  2. The platform prepares the appeal and files it with MEXC.
  3. The platform tracks the exchange's decision itself — you don't need to check anything manually. How long the decision takes depends on MEXC.

If the session expires or the proxy stops working in the meantime, the bot asks you to update the data (see Re-uploading).

docs.title: Statuses
docs.text:
While the executor is doing the face check, the slot shows the regular statuses. After that, it has its own:

Status What it means ⚙️ Appeal in progress The appeal is being prepared. Nothing is needed from you 📨 Appeal filed with MEXC The appeal has been sent and is awaiting the exchange's decision 📷 Repeat face check needed The face check has to be passed again — the same executor does it. Nothing is needed from you 🔁 Appeal rejected MEXC closed the appeal without lifting the restriction. Support decides the next steps ⚠️ Appeal error Something went wrong with the appeal, and support is handling it. Nothing is needed from you

docs.title: If MEXC says no
docs.text:
• The deposit screenshots were rejected — you'll get a notification with an "📸 Upload new screenshots" button; the slot card in the bot shows a "📸 New deposit screenshots" button, and the web app shows a "New deposit screenshots needed" block with a "Send screenshots" button. The new screenshots fully replace the old ones, and the appeal is filed again. You don't need to pay again.
  • The appeal was rejected — the status is "🔁 Appeal rejected". The order isn't closed on its own, and the money isn't refunded automatically. Support decides what to do next — file the appeal again, redo the face check or ask for new screenshots; if anything is needed from you, you'll get a notification. Sometimes MEXC lifts the restriction even after a rejection — support then closes the slot as completed.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Restriction lifted — you'll get a "✅ The restrictions on your account are lifted!" notification.
  • Restriction lifted with an observation period — the exchange may approve the request but keep some features restricted until a certain date; after that date, they're lifted automatically. You'll get a "✅ MEXC approved the appeal!" notification with that date.
  • Slot closed as completed by support — you'll get a notification that an administrator closed the slot as completed.

docs.title: Cancellation and refunds
docs.text:
Risk Removal has no fulfillment deadline, and a refusal from MEXC doesn't cancel the order or refund it automatically.

  • Until the executor has passed the first face check, the usual re-verification cancellation rules apply: you can cancel after 24 hours.
  • Once the first face check has passed, you can't cancel the order yourself — the cancel button disappears, and in the web app the slot card says: "This can no longer be cancelled here: the face check has passed and support is handling the slot now. To cancel it, contact support."
  • If MEXC doesn't require a face check for the account, you can't cancel the order yourself at all — support handles such a slot from the start. To cancel it, contact support.

If the executor hasn't started the face check yet and the account no longer has the restriction, the slot is closed with a full refund ("ℹ️ No check was needed — refunded"). Once a face check has been done or the appeal has been filed, nothing is refunded automatically — support decides what happens to the slot.

docs.title: Executors and order distribution
docs.text:
The verifications on the exchange are carried out by real people: executors (called "Sellers" in the interface). An executor passes the identity check through a link that the platform generates inside your session. Executors don't have your account's login details.

You can see who is working on a slot in its card: "👨‍💻 Executor: #…" in the workspace bot and "Worker" in the web app. The executor appears under the same number in the "Marketplace" section.

docs.title: Confirmed country
docs.text: When an executor registers, the platform compares the country of their phone number with their actual location. If the two match, the executor gets a confirmed country. As a result, your orders go first to people who are actually in the order's country, which improves the account's chances of passing future re-verifications.

docs.title: How an order finds an executor
docs.text:
Standard and wholesale orders go first to local executors whose confirmed country matches the order:

  1. First, the order is shown to your priority executors from that country.
  2. Then it's shown to all executors whose confirmed country matches the order.

A slot that returns to the pool goes through the same order again.

Executors you've blocked don't see your standard and wholesale orders.

Team orders are visible only to members of your team. A re-verification goes only to the executor who did the account's first verification (see Re-verifications).

docs.title: Executor's time and returning a slot to the pool
docs.text:
When an executor takes an initial verification slot, they have 4 hours of their own time to pass it. The time doesn't run while the slot is waiting for you to update its data or while the exchange is reviewing the verification. For team orders, you set this time yourself — see Worker's time per slot.

The slot card shows the time by which the executor has to finish: "⏳ The worker has until …" in the workspace bot, "Back to the pool by … at the latest" in the web app. If the slot deadline comes first, the card shows that instead.

A slot goes back to the pool if the executor runs out of time or gives the slot up themselves:

  • if they've already issued a verification link, the slot doesn't leave right away: the platform waits 10 minutes and checks the exchange — a passed verification counts;
  • after it's returned, the slot waits for an executor again; the previous executor can't take this particular slot again, but can take the order's other slots;
  • you don't pay anything extra, and the slot deadline, if you set one, doesn't start over;
  • if the account still passes through the link the previous executor issued, the slot goes back to them and counts as completed.

You can't swap the executor on a taken slot yourself: if they don't make it in time, the slot goes back to the pool on its own.

Re-verifications don't go back to the pool: they have no such time limit, and only the executor assigned to the account can do them.

docs.title: If an executor doesn't succeed
docs.text: If the exchange rejects an attempt, the executor retries on the same slot — nothing is needed from you. If the exchange gives a final refusal on the executor's attempt (for example, the document's country doesn't match the order's country), the slot is closed with a full refund — see Automatic refunds. Such a case counts as a failure for the executor.

docs.title: Quality control
docs.text: The platform monitors how well executors handle re-verifications. If an executor's re-verification success rate drops below the acceptable level, they automatically stop receiving new orders from the shared pool. This doesn't affect slots they've already taken, re-verifications assigned to them or team orders — you manage your own team yourself.

docs.title: Priority and blocking
docs.text:
In the web app, the "Sellers" screen has a "Marketplace" section. It lists executors who have taken slots of your standard and wholesale orders in the last 90 days, plus everyone you've already prioritized or blocked — even if they haven't worked for you in a long time. Members of your team aren't shown here. You can filter the list: "All", "Priority", "Blocked".

Action What it does "Prioritize" The executor sees your future orders in their confirmed country first. Available only for executors with a confirmed country "Remove" Removes the priority "Block" The executor no longer sees your standard and wholesale orders. Slots they've already taken, team orders and re-verifications of accounts they verified aren't affected "Unblock" Removes the block

An executor can be either prioritized or blocked, not both.

Note

Priority and blocking are available only in the web app.

docs.title: Executor's record
docs.text:
For each executor, you see only your own history with them, for all time: how many of your graded slots they passed and what share that is — for example, "12/13" and "92%". The platform doesn't show an overall executor rating.

Only finished slots are graded: those that passed and those closed through the executor's fault. Slots still in progress, slots returned to the pool, slots the executor gave up and closures that weren't their fault — for example, a slot deadline that ran out shortly after they took the slot — don't count. Until there are graded slots, the record shows "no slots yet".

The "Marketplace" counts all your orders except team orders; the "My team" section counts only team orders (see Team statistics).

docs.title: Subscription
docs.text: A subscription is paid access for a fixed period that unlocks wholesale prices and team orders.

docs.title: What a subscription gives you
docs.text:
• Wholesale prices — on the same catalog verifications, lower than the standard prices.
  • Team orders — orders for your team: any country and your own price per slot, all of which goes to the executor.

There's no limit on the number of orders: while your subscription is active, you can create as many wholesale and team orders as you like. Your subscription also affects re-verifications of accounts from wholesale and team orders: without one, re-verifying an account from a wholesale order costs the standard price, and re-verifying one from a team order isn't available.

docs.title: Plans
docs.text: The current plans, with their durations and prices, are shown in the workspace bot under "💳 Subscription" and in the web app under "Subscription". The plans differ only in duration — the access is the same.

docs.title: How to buy or renew
docs.text:
• Workspace bot — "💳 Subscription", then the plans button: "📋 Plans" if you've never had a subscription, "➕ Extend subscription" if it's active, or "➕ Renew" if it has expired. Choose a plan, tap "✅ Subscribe", check the confirmation card (plan, duration, price, balance, end date) and confirm.
  • Web app — the "Subscription" section: choose a plan under "Plans" ("Buy" or "Extend") and tap "Confirm & pay".

The payment is deducted from your balance. If you buy a plan while your current subscription is still active, the days are added to your current term. If your subscription has already expired, the new term starts from the moment you pay. Subscription purchases are non-refundable.

docs.title: When your subscription ends
docs.text:
Before your subscription ends, the workspace bot sends you two reminders: 3 days and 24 hours in advance. In the web app, during the last 3 days, a "Your subscription ends in …" strip with a "Renew" button appears at the top of the screen.

If your subscription ends in less than 24 hours, the bot and the web app warn you about it when you buy a wholesale or team order. It's only a warning — you can still place the order.

When the subscription ends, you get a "🚫 Your subscription has ended" notification. You can't buy new wholesale or team orders until you renew. Here's what happens to the orders you've already bought:

  • Slots an executor has already taken are fulfilled as usual.
  • Slots of published wholesale and team orders that nobody has taken are frozen: until you renew, the platform doesn't offer them to executors. If an executor hands a slot back after your subscription has ended, that slot is frozen too, and you get a separate notification about it.
  • Unpublished orders aren't frozen. But if you publish one without a subscription, its slots are frozen right away — the order card warns you about this.

Freezing only stops the slots from being offered to executors; everything else works as usual: you can upload accounts, update slot data when the platform asks for it and publish the order. Frozen slots are never cancelled on their own — they wait until you renew or cancel them. If the order has a slot deadline, it doesn't run while a slot is frozen: after renewal, it's moved forward by the time the slot spent frozen.

You can see how many slots are frozen on the subscription screen and on the order card (the "❄️ Frozen: N" line). With frozen slots, you can:

  • renew your subscription — in the "💳 Subscription" section or with the "Renew subscription" button on the order card. Frozen slots are offered to executors again right away, and the bot tells you how many;
  • cancel them — with the "Cancel frozen" button on the order card; see Frozen slots for how the refund works. Cancelled slots don't come back after renewal.

Freezing doesn't apply to:

  • standard orders — they don't depend on a subscription;
  • re-verifications — they're never frozen, even if the original order was a wholesale or team order.

docs.title: Your own team
docs.text:
Your own team is made up of executors you've invited personally. They fulfill your team orders, and you set the price per slot yourself. You can manage your team in the workspace bot @kycportal_bot ("👨‍💻 My team") and in the web app (the "Sellers" screen, "My team" section).

You can build and set up a team without a subscription, but team orders can only be created with an active subscription. Without a subscription, members don't get new slots of your orders — see When your subscription ends.

docs.title: Invitations
docs.text:
You have a personal invite link: in the workspace bot it's on the "👨‍💻 My team" screen, in the web app it's in the "Invite link" block. An executor opens it in Telegram and lands in the executors' bot. A new executor goes through a short registration there and joins your team right away.

  • A team can have up to 100 members, including paused ones.
  • The link doesn't expire. You can reissue it ("🔄 New link" in the bot, "New link" in the web app), and the old one stops working immediately.
  • If a member you've paused follows the link again, the pause isn't lifted — only you can bring them back.

docs.title: Member settings
docs.text:
For each member, you can set:

  • limits — how many slots they can take from one order and how many they can have in progress at the same time (or no limit). Re-verifications don't count toward the limits;
  • allowed countries — the countries for which they can take your orders (any country by default).

In the workspace bot, use the "📊 Limits" and "🌍 Countries" buttons on the member's card; in the web app, the "Slot limits" and "Allowed countries" blocks.

docs.title: Pausing and removing
docs.text:
• Pause ("⏸ Disable" in the bot, "Pause" in the web app) — the member temporarily can't see or take new slots of your team orders. They fulfill the slots they've already taken as usual, and re-verifications of accounts they verified still go to them. A pause can only be lifted manually: "▶️ Enable" in the bot or "Resume" in the web app.
  • Removal ("🗑 Remove from team") — the member can no longer take your team orders, and the current invite link stops working so they can't rejoin through it. In the bot, a new link appears on the "👨‍💻 My team" screen; in the web app, click "Create link". Slots the member has already taken aren't cancelled — they can finish them.

Re-verifications of accounts verified by a removed member wait for them: only they can do them. While they're off your team, such a re-verification, if nobody has taken it yet, can be cancelled right away, without waiting for the usual period (see Cancellations and refunds). If you add them back to the team, the waiting re-verifications go to them right away.

docs.title: Team orders
docs.text:
A team order is visible only to active members of your team (not paused), subject to their limits and allowed countries. Executors from the shared pool don't see it.

How to create one:

  • in the workspace bot — "➕ New order" → "For my team";
  • in the web app — "Create order" → "Team".

You choose the exchange and the country — any country, not just those in the catalog — and set the price per slot and the quantity. The full price per slot goes to the executor. When buying, you can optionally set a slot deadline. You need an active subscription and at least one active team member. If less than a day of your subscription is left, you'll see a warning before buying.

Re-verifications of accounts from team orders are done by the same member who did the first verification — see Re-verifications.

docs.title: Worker's time per slot
docs.text:
Each time a member takes a slot of a team order, they have a limited amount of time to pass the verification. If they don't make it, the slot goes back to your team's pool and another member can take it. That member can't take this particular slot again, but can take the order's other slots.

  • The default is 4 hours. You can choose 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 hours, or "No limit".
  • The time doesn't run while the slot is waiting for you to update its data or while the exchange is reviewing the verification.
  • 30 minutes before the time runs out, the member gets a reminder.
  • If the member has already issued a verification link, the platform first waits 10 minutes and checks the exchange: a passed verification counts.
  • Returning a slot to the pool doesn't count as a failure for the member.
  • A new value applies to slots members take after the change; the time on slots already taken doesn't change.

Where to set it: "⚙️ Settings" → "⏱ Worker's time" in the workspace bot, or "Settings" → "Worker's time per slot" in the web app (for no limit, turn off the "Enabled" switch). With no limit, the slot stays with the member until they complete it or until the slot deadline runs out, if you set one when buying.

This setting applies only to team orders. In standard and wholesale orders, the executor's time is set by the platform — see Executors and order distribution.

docs.title: When your subscription ends
docs.text:
Your team's members and settings are kept. Here's what happens to team orders:

  • slots members have already taken are fulfilled as usual — nothing is taken away from executors;
  • slots nobody has taken yet are frozen: members don't see them until you renew the subscription. If a member returns a slot to the pool after the subscription has ended (for example, they ran out of time), that slot is frozen too, and the bot will let you know;
  • the slot deadline of a frozen slot doesn't run — after renewal, it's moved forward by the time the slot was frozen;
  • you can still upload accounts and publish an order without a subscription — the slots will simply wait for renewal;
  • frozen slots can be cancelled — see Frozen slots;
  • new team orders can't be created without a subscription;
  • re-verifications already created are never frozen.

After renewal, frozen slots are offered to your team members again. See When your subscription ends for details.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
In the web app, on the "Sellers" screen in the "My team" section, you'll see:

  • "Members" — active and total;
  • "In progress" — how many slots members are working on right now;
  • "Success rate" and "Passed" — how many of the team's graded slots passed, as a percentage and as a count;
  • for each member — allowed countries, load (slots in progress against their limit), record and status.

The record covers only your team orders, for all time. How graded slots are counted is described in Executor's record.

In the workspace bot, the "👨‍💻 My team" screen shows the total number of members and how many of them are active. Detailed team analytics are available in the web app, in the "Analytics" section.

docs.title: Uploading accounts
docs.text:
For the platform to carry out a verification, you need to upload the following to each slot in the order:

  • the account's session — cookies from a browser that is logged in to the exchange account;
  • a proxy — a separate one for each account.

The verification runs inside your session: the executor doesn't log in to the account separately and never receives the login details. Uploading works the same way in the workspace bot @kycportal_bot (the "📤 Upload accounts" or "📤 Upload all accounts" button on the order card) and in the web app.

docs.title: ADS Power
docs.text:
If you manage your accounts in ADS Power:

  1. Log in to the accounts you need in ADS Power.
  2. Close the profiles you're going to export.
  3. Export them to .txt. The file must contain cookies for every profile; the proxy and user-agent are also taken from the file if they're included.
  4. Send the file to the bot ("📦 ADS Power (.txt)") or upload it in the web app ("ADS Power file").

Each profile in the file fills one slot. If the file has more accounts than there are free slots in the order, the extra ones are skipped, and you get a separate message about it. One upload takes at most 200 accounts — for a large order, split the file and send the parts one after another.

docs.title: Manually
docs.text:
You provide the proxy and cookies separately for each account:

  • in the bot — "📁 Manual (proxy + cookies)": first a list of proxies (one per line), then a cookies file (.json or .txt) for each slot in turn. The bot checks the proxies right away and shows each one's country. If an account fails its check because of the proxy, you can send a new proxy for that slot as a single line at the cookies step;
  • in the web app — "Manual": a card for each account, with a proxy line and a cookies field.

Proxies and cookies are matched in order: the first proxy line goes to the first account, and so on.

Cookie formats:

  • a JSON array of cookie objects — the standard export from a browser extension;
  • a JSON object {"name": "value"} or a {"cookies": [...]} wrapper;
  • a string in Cookie header format: name=value; name2=value2;
  • a single token like xxx.yyy.zzz.

Proxy formats:

  • host:port
  • host:port:user:pass
  • user:pass@host:port
  • scheme://[user:pass@]host:port

You don't have to specify the protocol — the platform detects it automatically. Local and internal addresses (such as 127.0.0.1 or 192.168.x.x) aren't accepted.

docs.title: Account checks
docs.text:
Every upload — by file or manual — is sent as a batch. The platform checks each account on the exchange and reports the result for each one. The check may take a while:

  • it runs on the platform's side: in the web app you can close the page and come back later — the result is kept; in the bot, if the check takes long, the result arrives as a separate message;
  • if a platform update interrupts the check, it resumes on its own, and accounts already accepted aren't lost. If the check does stop early, you'll see how many accounts were saved — send the rest again (in the web app, "Upload remaining");
  • while the platform is checking one file for an order, you can't send another file for the same order — wait for the result.

If some accounts are accepted and others aren't, send a file with only the rejected ones — accepted slots aren't affected. The error list gives each account's position in your file and its ADS Power profile name, so they're easy to find. If you lose track, start from scratch: "🔁 Start over (reset everything)" in the bot, "Start over" in the web app.

Warning

"🔁 Start over (reset everything)" removes every accepted account from the order, and you'll have to redo the whole upload. In the web app, "Start over" clears the slots once the next file is accepted.

docs.title: Replacing accounts before publishing
docs.text:
Until the order is published, you can open any slot and replace its account: "✏️ Edit this slot" in the bot, or the "Edit slot" block on the slot card in the web app (where you can also change just the proxy). If the new account fails its check, the slot keeps the old one.

"✏️ Edit all slots" in the bot and "Re-upload all accounts" in the web app start the upload from scratch: once the file is accepted, every slot is cleared and refilled from it in order. A slot whose account fails its check stays empty, and an order with an empty slot can't be published. For publishing, see Orders.

docs.title: Can the verification start now
docs.text:
When you upload an account to an initial verification order, the platform asks the exchange whether a verification can start on that account right now. The account is accepted only if the exchange allows it — including after a rejected attempt, if the exchange allows another one. Otherwise the account is rejected, and the slot stays free for a different account. The reasons for a refusal:

  • the account has already passed verification;
  • the exchange no longer allows verification on this account;
  • the account has used up its daily verification attempts — you can upload it again in about a day;
  • a verification is already under review on the account — wait for its result.

What can be known in advance depends on the exchange: KuCoin only reports that an account is already verified, so on KuCoin only such accounts are rejected. There's no such check when you re-upload.

If the exchange stops allowing a verification after the order is published (for example, the account has used up its attempts) and no verification link has been issued to an executor for the slot yet, the slot is cancelled with a full refund, and the notification names the reason.

docs.title: Exchange specifics
docs.text:
• MEXC — if the exchange's main domain doesn't open for you, log in through an alternative domain (for example, mexc.fm). The platform detects which domain the cookies came from and works through that domain.
  • Bybit — sessions only last a limited time, so export the cookies right before uploading.
  • KuCoin — browser profiles pick up unrelated cookies especially easily. Use a dedicated profile that has only ever opened KuCoin.

docs.title: Re-uploading
docs.text: Once the order is published, you can't change a slot's account or proxy. The exceptions are when the platform itself asks for fresh data, and when you replace a proxy the exchange doesn't open through (see below).

docs.title: When the platform asks for data
docs.text:
The platform works with the account only through your session and your proxy. If it turns out the session has expired or the proxy has stopped responding, the slot moves to "⚠️ Data update required", and the bot sends you a message — for a single slot or as a summary for several. If the data still hasn't arrived after 6 hours, you get one reminder. These messages can't be turned off in the notification settings.

Before asking for a new proxy, the platform checks whether the proxy works at all. If the proxy works and only the exchange won't open, no new data is requested.

docs.title: While the slot is waiting
docs.text:
The slot is paused:

  • no clock runs: not your deadline, not the executor's time, and not the MEXC face-check deadline;
  • the slot isn't cancelled and doesn't move to another executor automatically;
  • you can't check the slot's status. Cancelling a re-verification becomes available after the update, and cancelling a frozen slot that already had a verification link issued waits for the update — only then does the platform check the exchange.

If you had an open request to cancel a re-verification and the pause dropped it, the data-update message says so — you can send the request again after the update.

docs.title: What to upload
docs.text:
Upload exactly what's requested. In the bot, tap "🔄 Re-upload" on the slot card or the button in the message itself ("↩️ Update proxy", "↩️ Re-upload session", "↩️ Update slot"), then choose a method — ADS Power or manual.

What's needed In the bot In the web app Proxy One new proxy "Replace proxy" Cookies Fresh cookies; the saved proxy stays "Re-upload cookies" Proxy and cookies A new proxy and a fresh session "Re-upload proxy & cookies"

Re-upload requirements:

  • the session must be from the same account that was in the slot — a session from a different account will be rejected;
  • you update one slot at a time: one proxy (a list of several lines isn't accepted), and for ADS Power uploads, an export with exactly one account;
  • the bot handles one upload at a time: if you start updating another slot, the previous upload is cancelled, and the bot tells you so.

If the slot came to need more while you were getting the data ready — for example, you sent a new proxy and it turned out the session had expired too — the slot asks for both the proxy and the cookies. Send them together.

Once the update succeeds, work on the slot resumes immediately, from where it stopped: the slot returns to its previous status, and its clocks to the time they had left before the pause. If the slot was left without an executor during the pause, it goes back to the queue for executors.

docs.title: The exchange doesn't open through your proxy
docs.text:
Sometimes the proxy works, but the provider's network blocks the exchange. If "🔍 Check status" answered "🌐 Your proxy works, but the exchange doesn't open through it…", you can replace the proxy yourself: "🔌 Replace proxy" on the slot card (in the web app, "Replace proxy" under the check's answer). The slot pauses until the new proxy arrives — tap "🔄 Re-upload" and send the proxy.

If the same thing comes up while re-uploading cookies, the bot offers to take a new proxy too, and the web app shows a "Send a new proxy too" switch.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep a separate browser profile for each exchange, and close the ADS Power profile before exporting it.
  • Don't use the same proxy for two different accounts.
  • Export cookies shortly before uploading, especially for Bybit.
  • Don't upload an account that has already passed the verification you're ordering, or one that already has a verification under review.

docs.title: Web app
docs.text: The web app is a browser application with the same data as the workspace bot: your orders, balance, team and subscription. It isn't a Telegram Mini App: it opens in a regular browser on your computer or phone.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
1. In the workspace bot @kycportal_bot, tap "🌐 Open in browser" or send /browser. This only works in a private chat with the bot.
  2. The bot sends you a one-time link. It's valid for 3 minutes.
  3. Tap the link to copy it, then paste it into the browser you normally use. The button under the message opens the app right away, but on a phone it opens in Telegram's built-in browser — and you'll stay signed in only there.
  4. The first time you sign in on a browser, the app shows which account you've signed in to. Check that it's yours and tap "Continue as …"; if it isn't your account, tap "Sign out".
  5. Once you've signed in, the browser remembers you, so you don't need a new link every time. A sign-in lasts up to 7 days, and ends sooner if you don't open the app for 48 hours. After that, you'll need a new link from the bot.

If you open the link in a browser that's already signed in, the app warns you and lets you choose: "Stay signed in as …" or "Continue with the new link". If you didn't request the link yourself, stay in your current account.

Warning

The sign-in link works only once and is issued to you personally — don't forward it.

To sign out, use "Log out" in the account menu or go to "Settings" → "Session": "Log out" signs you out of the current browser, and "Log out all devices" signs you out everywhere at once. To sign in again, you'll need a new link from the bot.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Dashboard — the verification catalog: exchanges, countries and prices, with a "Buy" button (with an active subscription, it shows wholesale prices). Alongside it: your subscription status, a warning when slots are waiting for your action (a re-upload, a proxy or new screenshots), recent orders, your balance with "Top up" and "Transactions" buttons, key figures (slots in progress and waiting for an executor, verifications done, spend over 30 days) and your referral link.

Analytics — metrics for your orders over 7, 30 or 90 days or all time, broken down into "All", "Team" and "Global" (the shared pool): verification success rate, average time waiting for an executor and average time to complete, failure reasons, verification trends, pass rates by exchange and country, and team productivity.

docs.title: Verifications
docs.text:
Create order — three modes: "Catalog" (an exchange and a country at catalog prices; with an active subscription you choose the wholesale or the standard price), "Team" and "Reverification". For catalog and team orders you can set a slot deadline: "No deadline", a preset from 4 to 72 hours, or "Other…" — any whole number of hours within that range. The deadline can't be changed after purchase — see Fulfillment deadline. After payment, the "Upload accounts" button opens the upload — using an ADS Power file or manually. See Orders, Uploading accounts and Re-verifications.

Orders — all your orders, with filters by status, exchange, country, type and period, and search by order or slot number. An order card shows its slots, the full event history and actions: uploading and re-uploading accounts, publishing, cancelling an unpublished order, and — when slots are frozen — renewing the subscription or cancelling those slots.

Slots — a single list of all your accounts, regardless of the order they belong to. A slot card shows the status, outcome, time left and the actions available at that moment: check the status, replace the proxy or update the session, send new deposit screenshots for Risk Removal, cancel a re-verification and, on a completed slot, "Create a re-verification". See Order execution and deadlines.

docs.title: Team
docs.text:
Sellers — two sections: "My team" (see Your own team) and "Marketplace", where you prioritize and block executors (see Executors and order distribution).

Subscription — buying and renewing and a price comparison; after a subscription ends, how many slots are waiting for the renewal. See Subscription.

docs.title: Money
docs.text:
Balance — your deposit address, the minimum amount, networks and deposit history. See Balance and top-ups.

Transactions — the full history of operations: top-ups, payments, refunds and bonuses, with filters and a detail card for each operation.

Affiliate — your referral link, statistics and bonus history. See Referral program.

docs.title: Help and settings
docs.text:
Help & Support — video guides ("Uploading from ADS Power", "Manual upload", "Video guide"), documents ("Documentation", "FAQ", "Terms of Use") and a "Chat with support" button. There's also a "Got an idea?" form for suggestions — you won't get a reply to it.

Settings (in the account menu):

  • "Account" — which Telegram account you're signed in with;
  • "Appearance" — theme (light, dark or system) and language;
  • "Notifications" — which notifications to push to Telegram: "Per slot", "Per order", "Deposits" and "Referral bonuses", each on its own;
  • "Worker's time per slot" — for team orders: from 1 to 24 hours or no limit (see Getting started and Your own team);
  • "Session" — sign out of the current browser or all devices.
